grinning-face: A big, plain smile used to show you are happy, friendly or in a good mood.
grinning-face-with-big-eyes: An open, excited smile for good news, enthusiasm or a cheerful greeting.
grinning-face-with-smiling-eyes: A warm, laughing smile used for joy, amusement or a happy reaction to something.
beaming-face-with-smiling-eyes: A wide grin showing teeth, used for pride, delight or a cheeky kind of happiness. Some people also use it for an awkward, nervous smile.
grinning-squinting-face: A face laughing so hard its eyes are squeezed shut, used when something is really funny.
grinning-face-with-sweat: A smile with a drop of sweat, used for relief, nervous laughter or an awkward moment you got through.
rolling-on-the-floor-laughing: Laughing so hard you are rolling on the floor: a stronger "that is hilarious" than 😂.
face-with-tears-of-joy: Laughing until you cry: the everyday way to say something is very funny.
slightly-smiling-face: A small, polite smile. It can be friendly, but many people read it as forced or passive-aggressive.
upside-down-face: A smile turned upside down, used for sarcasm, silliness or putting on a brave face when things are going wrong.
melting-face: A smiling face melting into a puddle, used for embarrassment, being overwhelmed, or feeling the heat.
winking-face: A wink, used to show you are joking, flirting a little or sharing a secret.
smiling-face-with-smiling-eyes: A gentle, blushing smile for warmth, thanks, happiness or feeling pleased.
smiling-face-with-halo: A smile with a halo, used to look innocent, to mark a good deed, or to pretend to be well behaved.
smiling-face-with-hearts: A smiling face surrounded by hearts, used to show love, affection or feeling adored.
smiling-face-with-heart-eyes: Heart-shaped eyes for loving something or someone: a person, a photo, food, a song.
star-struck: Star-shaped eyes, used when you are amazed, excited or starstruck by something or someone.
face-blowing-a-kiss: Blowing a kiss, used to say goodbye or goodnight with love, or to thank someone warmly.
smiling-face: A calm, content smile, used for gentle happiness or a polite, friendly tone.
kissing-face-with-closed-eyes: A kiss with closed eyes, used for affection between partners, family or close friends.
kissing-face-with-smiling-eyes: A light, cheerful kiss, also used for whistling or a carefree mood.
smiling-face-with-tear: Smiling with a tear, used for mixed feelings: touched, proud, relieved, or laughing through something sad.
face-savoring-food: Licking its lips, used for delicious food or something that looks tempting.
face-with-tongue: Sticking out its tongue, used for playful teasing, jokes or a silly mood.
winking-face-with-tongue: A wink with the tongue out, used for joking around, being goofy or not taking something seriously.
zany-face: A wild, goofy face, used for being crazy in a fun way, excited or silly.
squinting-face-with-tongue: Tongue out with eyes squeezed shut, used for teasing, playful disgust or acting silly.
smiling-face-with-open-hands: Meant as a hug, used to send warmth, comfort or thanks. Some people read the hands as jazz hands instead.
face-with-hand-over-mouth: Covering its mouth, used for a giggle, surprise, or "oops" after saying something awkward.
face-with-peeking-eye: Peeking through its fingers, used when something is scary, embarrassing or too awkward to watch.
shushing-face: A finger on the lips, used to ask for quiet or to keep something a secret.
thinking-face: A hand on the chin, used when you are thinking, unsure, or doubtful about something.
saluting-face: A salute, used to say "yes, sir", to accept a task, or to show respect, sometimes jokingly.
face-with-raised-eyebrow: One raised eyebrow, used for doubt, suspicion or disbelief.
neutral-face: A straight face, used for being unimpressed, speechless or deliberately showing no reaction.
expressionless-face: Eyes shut and a flat mouth, used for annoyance, exasperation or "I have no words".
face-without-mouth: A face with no mouth, used for being speechless, keeping quiet or having nothing to say.
smirking-face: A sly smirk, used for confidence, mischief, flirting or a knowing look.
unamused-face: A sideways, unimpressed look, used for annoyance, disapproval or boredom.
face-with-rolling-eyes: Rolling its eyes, used for annoyance, sarcasm or disbelief at something silly.
grimacing-face: Clenched teeth, used for awkward or uncomfortable moments, nervousness or "yikes".
relieved-face: A calm face with closed eyes, used for relief, contentment or feeling at peace.
pensive-face: A sad, thoughtful look downwards, used for disappointment, regret or feeling down.
sleepy-face: A face with a bubble from its nose, as cartoons show sleep, used for being tired or sleepy. Some read the bubble as a tear.
drooling-face: Drooling, used for wanting something badly, often tasty food or something you really like.
sleeping-face: Asleep with a "zzz", used for being tired, going to bed, or finding something boring.
face-with-medical-mask: Wearing a medical mask, used for being ill, staying healthy or talking about colds and flu.
hot-face: A red, sweating face, used for hot weather, spicy food, or saying someone looks attractive.
cold-face: A blue, freezing face, used for cold weather, feeling chilly, or a cold, harsh reaction.
face-with-crossed-out-eyes: Crossed-out eyes, used for shock, exhaustion, being dizzy or "I'm dead" after something funny or surprising.
cowboy-hat-face: A smiling face in a cowboy hat, used for a fun, carefree mood, country style or a playful "howdy".
partying-face: A party hat and a party horn, used for birthdays, celebrations and good news.
smiling-face-with-sunglasses: Wearing sunglasses, used for being cool, confident or relaxed, or for sunny weather.
nerd-face: Glasses and buck teeth, used for being nerdy, studious, or teasing someone who is showing off what they know.
confused-face: A puzzled face, used when something is unclear or you are not sure what to make of it.
worried-face: A worried look, used for concern, nervousness or anxiety about something.
slightly-frowning-face: A small frown, used for mild sadness, disappointment or concern.
frowning-face: A full frown, used for sadness, disappointment or displeasure.
face-with-open-mouth: An open mouth, used for surprise, shock or being impressed.
astonished-face: Wide eyes and an open mouth, used for amazement, shock or disbelief.
flushed-face: A blushing face with wide eyes, used for embarrassment, surprise or being flustered.
pleading-face: Big, shiny eyes, used to beg nicely, to look cute, or when something is touching.
face-holding-back-tears: Trying not to cry, used for being moved, grateful or proud, and sometimes for being sad but brave.
fearful-face: A scared face, used for fear, shock or dread.
anxious-face-with-sweat: Sweating with an open mouth, used for stress, anxiety or panic.
sad-but-relieved-face: A face with a drop of sweat or a tear, used for sadness, disappointment or relief after a scare.
crying-face: A single tear, used for sadness, hurt feelings or being touched.
loudly-crying-face: Sobbing with streams of tears, used for deep sadness, but just as often for being overwhelmed: by laughter, by something cute, or by happiness.
face-screaming-in-fear: Hands on cheeks, screaming, used for shock, fear or extreme surprise.
confounded-face: A scrunched, frustrated face, used for being upset, stressed or confused.
persevering-face: Eyes squeezed shut, used for struggling through something hard, frustration or holding on.
disappointed-face: Eyes closed and a frown, used for disappointment, sadness or regret.
downcast-face-with-sweat: Looking down with cold sweat, used for stress, hard work or a letdown.
weary-face: A tired, distressed face, used for exhaustion, frustration, or being overwhelmed by something.
tired-face: An exhausted face, used for being worn out, fed up or upset.
face-with-steam-from-nose: Steam puffing from its nose, used for anger or frustration, but also for pride and triumph.
enraged-face: A red, furious face, used for strong anger.
angry-face: A frowning, angry face, used for annoyance or anger.
face-with-symbols-on-mouth: Symbols over its mouth, standing for swearing, used for great anger or frustration.
smiling-face-with-horns: A purple face with horns and a grin, used for mischief, naughty plans or playful bad behaviour.
skull: A skull, used literally for death or Halloween, and very often to mean "I'm dead": something is so funny or embarrassing that you could die.
cat-with-tears-of-joy: A cat laughing until it cries: the cat version of 😂, for something very funny.
smiling-cat-with-heart-eyes: A cat with heart eyes, used for loving something, often cats or something cute.
see-no-evil-monkey: A monkey covering its eyes, used for embarrassment, "I can't look", or playful shyness.
speak-no-evil-monkey: A monkey covering its mouth, used for "oops, I shouldn't have said that" or keeping a secret.
heart-with-arrow: A heart pierced by Cupid's arrow, used for falling in love, crushes and Valentine's Day.
heart-with-ribbon: A heart tied with a ribbon, used for love given as a gift, Valentine's Day or a sweet gesture.
sparkling-heart: A sparkling pink heart, used for love, affection, excitement or something sweet.
growing-heart: A heart that seems to grow, used for growing love, excitement or a heart full of feeling.
beating-heart: A beating heart, used for love, excitement or a racing heart.
revolving-hearts: Two hearts circling each other, used for love between two people.
two-hearts: Two pink hearts, used for love, affection and friendship, often casually.
heart-decoration: A heart inside a square, used as a decoration for love or affection.
heart-exclamation: A heart used as an exclamation mark, used to show strong agreement or love.
broken-heart: A heart broken in two, used for heartbreak, sadness, or a breakup.
red-heart: The classic red heart, used for love, thanks and support, and to like a message.
orange-heart: An orange heart, used for love and care, often a bit less intense than ❤️, and for autumn or anything orange.
yellow-heart: A yellow heart, used for friendship, happiness and positive feelings.
green-heart: A green heart, used for nature, health, growth, and anything green.
blue-heart: A blue heart, used for trust, calm and friendship, and for anything blue.
purple-heart: A purple heart, used for love, support and compassion; fans of some groups use it as their colour.
black-heart: A black heart, used for grief and dark humour, or for black-themed style.
kiss-mark: A lipstick kiss mark, used for kisses, love and flirting, or for make-up.
hundred-points: "100" underlined, used to say "exactly", "totally agree" or "perfect".
anger-symbol: A comic-style anger mark, used for annoyance or anger.
collision: A collision or explosion, used for something sudden, exciting or impressive, or for a crash.
dizzy: A star with a curved trail, used for feeling dizzy, but also for something magical or sparkling.
sweat-droplets: Drops of water or sweat, used for sweating, splashing, rain or hard work. Some people use it suggestively.
dashing-away: A puff of air or dust, used for running off fast, a sigh, or wind.
waving-hand: A waving hand, used to say hello or goodbye.
raised-hand: A raised hand, used for "stop", a high five, or putting your hand up.
ok-hand: Thumb and finger in a circle, used for "OK", "perfect" or approval.
pinched-fingers: Fingertips pinched together, an Italian hand gesture, used to ask "what do you mean?" or for something perfect.
victory-hand: Two fingers in a V, used for victory, peace, or as a pose in photos.
crossed-fingers: Crossed fingers, used for hoping for good luck.
love-you-gesture: The "I love you" hand sign from American Sign Language, used for love, or for a rock-and-roll feel.
sign-of-the-horns: The horns hand sign, used for rock music, metal and excitement.
call-me-hand: The "call me" sign, also used as the shaka sign for "hang loose" and a relaxed, surfer vibe.
backhand-index-pointing-left: A finger pointing left, used to point to something on the left or earlier in a message.
backhand-index-pointing-right: A finger pointing right, used to point to a link, an image or what comes next.
backhand-index-pointing-down: A finger pointing down, used to point to a link, a post or something below.
index-pointing-up: A finger pointing up, used for "this" (pointing to the message above), or to make a point.
thumbs-up: A thumbs-up, used for approval, agreement, "OK" or "good job". In some places and situations it can read as curt or dismissive.
thumbs-down: A thumbs-down, used for disapproval, disagreement or "no".
raised-fist: A raised fist, used for strength, solidarity, support and resistance.
oncoming-fist: A fist coming at you, used as a fist bump, for agreement or congratulations, or for a punch.
clapping-hands: Clapping hands, used for applause, praise and congratulations, and sometimes sarcastically.
raising-hands: Two raised hands, used for celebrating, cheering, or "hooray".
heart-hands: Hands making a heart, used to send love and thanks to someone.
palms-up-together: Open hands held up together, used for prayer, asking for something, or offering.
handshake: A handshake, used for agreement, a deal, a greeting or respect.
folded-hands: Two hands pressed together, used to say please or thank you, for praying or hope, or as a respectful greeting. Some people read it as a high five.
flexed-biceps: A flexed arm, used for strength, the gym, effort or "you can do it".
eyes: A pair of eyes looking sideways, used for "I'm watching", curiosity, or to show something deserves attention.
baby: A baby, used for babies, pregnancy news, or calling someone cute.
person-gesturing-no: A person crossing their arms in an X, used for "no", "not allowed" or "stop".
person-gesturing-ok: A person with arms forming an O over their head, used for "OK" or "yes".
person-tipping-hand: A person with a palm up near the shoulder, used for sass, a confident "just saying", or offering information.
person-raising-hand: A person raising a hand, used for "me!", asking a question or volunteering.
person-facepalming: A hand slapped to the face, used for disbelief, frustration or embarrassment at something silly.
person-shrugging: A shrug, used for "I don't know", "I don't care" or "whatever".
person-walking: A person walking, used for walking, going somewhere or leaving.
person-running: A person running, used for running, exercise, or being in a hurry.
woman-dancing: A woman dancing in a red dress, used for dancing, parties, celebrating and feeling great.
man-dancing: A man dancing, used for dancing, parties and celebrating.
speaking-head: A silhouette of a speaking head, used for speaking out, shouting, or sharing an opinion.
dog-face: A dog's face, used for dogs, pets, and being cute or loyal.
butterfly: A butterfly, used for nature, beauty, change and growth, and for feeling nervous ("butterflies").
bouquet: A bouquet of flowers, used for congratulations, thanks, birthdays, love and apologies.
cherry-blossom: A pink cherry blossom, used for spring, beauty and things that are cute or gentle.
rose: A red rose, used for love, romance and appreciation.
hibiscus: A hibiscus flower, used for tropical places, summer, beauty and holidays.
sunflower: A sunflower, used for happiness, sunshine, summer and positive feelings.
blossom: A small yellow flower, used for nature, spring and cheerful messages.
tulip: A tulip, used for spring, flowers, love and kindness.
seedling: A sprouting plant, used for growth, new beginnings and nature.
herb: A sprig of leaves, used for plants, nature, herbs and healthy living.
four-leaf-clover: A four-leaf clover, used for good luck and Saint Patrick's Day.
leaf-fluttering-in-wind: Leaves blowing in the wind, used for wind, nature, calm or a fresh feeling.
strawberry: A strawberry, used for the fruit, summer, sweetness and cute things.
birthday-cake: A birthday cake with candles, used for birthdays and celebrations.
hot-beverage: A steaming cup, used for coffee, tea, a morning drink, or "tea" meaning gossip.
beer-mug: A mug of beer, used for beer, drinks and going out.
clinking-beer-mugs: Two beer mugs clinking, used for "cheers", drinking with friends and celebrating.
police-car-light: A flashing police light, used for alerts, emergencies and "warning", often jokingly.
airplane: An airplane, used for flights, travel and holidays.
new-moon-face: A dark moon with a face, often read as sly, awkward or creepy, used for mischief or strange moments.
sun: The sun, used for sunny weather, summer and good mornings.
sun-with-face: A smiling sun, used for sunshine, good mornings and cheerful moods.
star: A yellow star, used for stars, ratings, favourites and something excellent.
glowing-star: A glowing star, used for something amazing, a star performer or a magical moment.
rainbow: A rainbow, used for rainbows, hope, joy, and pride and LGBTQ+ support.
high-voltage: A lightning bolt, used for electricity, energy, speed, and something exciting.
fire: Flames, used for fire and heat, and very often for something great, hot or exciting ("that's fire").
sparkles: Sparkles, used for something new, clean, special or magical, and to add emphasis to words.
balloon: A balloon, used for parties, birthdays and celebrations.
party-popper: A party popper, used for celebrations, congratulations and good news.
confetti-ball: A ball bursting with confetti, used for celebrations and congratulations.
ribbon: A pink bow, used for gifts, cute style and decoration.
wrapped-gift: A wrapped present, used for gifts, birthdays, holidays and surprises.
trophy: A trophy, used for winning, prizes, success and achievements.
soccer-ball: A football (soccer ball), used for the sport, matches and fans.
heart-suit: The heart from a deck of cards, used for cards and games, and often as another love heart.
crown: A crown, used for royalty, winning, and calling someone the king or queen of something.
gem-stone: A cut gem, used for diamonds, jewellery, luxury, and something precious.
musical-note: A musical note, used for music, songs and singing.
musical-notes: Two musical notes, used for music, songs, singing and humming.
money-bag: A bag of money, used for money, wealth, prices and getting paid.
money-with-wings: Banknotes with wings, used for spending, losing money or money flying away.
warning: A warning sign, used for caution, warnings and "be careful".
right-arrow: An arrow pointing right, used to point to the next thing, a link, or for "go".
down-arrow: An arrow pointing down, used to point to something below, such as a link.
play-button: A play button, used for videos, music, or "start".
double-exclamation-mark: Two exclamation marks, used for strong emphasis, surprise or excitement.
red-question-mark: A red question mark, used to ask a question or show confusion.
red-exclamation-mark: A red exclamation mark, used for emphasis, alerts and important points.
check-mark-button: A green box with a check mark, used for done, correct, approved or a completed task.
check-mark: A check mark, used for yes, correct, done or a ticked item on a list.
cross-mark: A red cross, used for no, wrong, cancelled or not allowed.
red-circle: A red circle, used for a red dot, recording, live broadcasts, alerts and anything red.
